extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media-criticism readers, and general readers interested in ethics of celebrity coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and editorial criteria for producing ethical, trustworthy celebrity profile interviews (including handling when the subject is unavailable and when using AI). Focuses on authenticity, question quality, editorial judgment, transparency, and sensitivity toward subjects and their fans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate interviews / authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine made the whole fucking thing up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing invented answers presented as an interview is a fundamental journalistic failure. Avoid presenting AI-generated or invented material as if it were real responses from the subject; fabrication undermines trust and is ethically unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you lack access to the subject, spike the piece rather than fake it
rubrics_metrics.description: From the basic idea that you wouldn’t just spike the whole piece due to scheduling issues...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a scheduled profile lacks access to the interview subject, the responsible option is to cancel or postpone publication instead of fabricating content. Editors should prefer absence over deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask thoughtful, interesting questions — don't rely on lazy prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparent belief that Esquire Singapore was incapable of coming up with questions interesting enough to baffle a half-assed Claude drone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and interviewers must craft questions that elicit insight; poor or perfunctory prompts that produce banal AI output are an editorial failing. Relying on AI to substitute for substantive questioning leads to cookie-cutter answers and worthless copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let AI speak for the subject without careful ethical consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine took a bunch of Mackenyu’s old interview answers, ran them through an AI, and then pelted the language model with their own questions, generating a laundry list of banal, cookie cutter 'answers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using AI to generate a subject's voice risks misrepresentation. If AI is used to simulate a person's responses, that must be avoided or clearly and responsibly framed; editors should not let synthetic responses substitute for the subject's voice or agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative or ghoulish angles about sensitive family/legacy issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial myopia involved in reading the 'AI Mackenyu' speculate on the 29-year-old’s relationship to the legacy of his late father, acclaimed martial arts actor Sonny Chiba, and not thinking, 'Hey, even for an inherently ghoulish concept, this should probably be cut.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exploit or speculate about a subject's personal tragedies or deceased relatives for lurid effect. Material that fetishizes or sensationalizes sensitive family matters should be removed in editorial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight: cut content that is ethically or tastefully wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: The resulting piece is a staggering success in the field of journalistic and editorial failure... this should probably be cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors bear responsibility to recognize and excise ghoulish, exploitative, or unethical content. Strong editorial gatekeeping must be applied before publication to prevent reputational and ethical harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing something as 'artistic expression' or an 'experiment' does not absolve ethical lapses
rubrics_metrics.description: Esquire Singapore posits this as some sort of artistic expression on the unknowability of celebrity and the inherent distance of interviewing famous people; as reporters... our response to that can only be a hearty, and vigorous, 'Hey, go fuck yourself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claiming experimental or artistic intent does not excuse deception, exploitation, or poor standards. Framing must not be used to justify unethical practices; editors should ensure that any experimental method is explicitly ethical and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the subject’s fanbase and likely reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mackenyu’s extremely vocal fanbase is not happy, apparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about how a subject’s community will react and whether publication may cause harm or significant backlash. Audience and fan reaction are practical indicators of ethical or reputational risk that editors should weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about methods is required and must be meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: A meandering introductory note to the piece attempts to make this ghoulish little desperation play sound like a bold philosophical experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonstandard methods (e.g., using AI, simulations) are used, disclose them clearly and prominently. A perfunctory or opaque note is insufficient; transparency should allow readers to understand what is real, what is generated, and why the approach was chosen.
